Primary means a pump, its components, or directly connected drive/piping/protection explicitly within the document's pump application. Generic reliability or rotating-equipment knowledge without a stated pump link is background. Other equipment-specific facts are out_of_scope. Retain these distinctions; do not invent pump instances. All 15 relations remain available, but core coverage concerns only the 11 marked core_diagnostic_relation. Nonrepresentable facts or unresolved mappings belong in auxiliary or unresolved as {statement, reason, evidence_text, evidence_unit_ids}; their existence does not license inventing a positive relation. An empty assertions array is valid. Produce each atomic assertion once. Independent action targets may be split; retain prerequisites and sequence so fragments are not presented as complete safe procedures. Do not treat synonymous phrasing as distinct facts.

A conditional statement is not an unconditional edge. A checklist question asking whether something holds is an inspection, not automatically a conditional rule.
2. Keep cause direction, uncertainty, recommendation strength, and negation. A probable cause is not a necessary cause or a unique reverse diagnosis. Keep explicit exceptions even when a table-wide title suggests a default action.

5. Check for omitted source-supported core assertions across the full page without adding facts from background knowledge, and separate procedure titles from concrete atomic steps.

{"doc_id": "MP006", "pdf_page_number": 6, "title": "Guidelines for Pump Installation", "pump_type": "centrifugal_pump", "service": "pump_installation", "applicability_scope": "安装机理可用于相同结构泵组;不得扩展为所有泵型的故障事实", "document_sha256": "A9EEFAD74A30658283F95C36EC477693BA8AB482471290CF12CAE69C95F764F3", "page_text_sha256": "3278e1c7cdbf0cc3b2db171a4cc132c825e94b10d8eaa42a51db377f34ea6c02", "page_text": "                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
     Instruction        for   installing       pumps                              
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
     with    flange      support(s)                                               
                                                                                  
     (also applies to horizontal pumps)                                           
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
     1. Fasten the pump to the underlying structure (= foundation / concrete plinth / floor) and check that the pump is level.
                                                                                  
     2. Check that the pump shaft can be rotated freely - i.e. by hand without noise and abnormal resistance.
                                                                                  
     3. Place flange support(s) at the pump’s flange(s) and check that the bolt holes are aligned and that the gasket surfaces
       are parallel.                                                              
     4. If the underlying structure is not level (plane), it may be necessary to shim under either the pump footplate or under
       the flange support(s).                                                     
                                                                                  
     5. Insert gasket(s) between pump and flange support(s) and hold together and parallel with 4 temporary bolts 90° offset
       in each flange.                                                            
                                                                                  
     6. Check that the flange support(s) have full contact with the underlying structure (if there is more than a 0.5 mm air gap
       under the feet, shims must be placed underneath)                           
     7. Bolt flange support(s) to underlying structure.                           
                                                                                  
     8. Remove the 4 temporary bolts and mount the pipe system flange(s) and gasket(s) against the flange support(s).
                                                                                  
     9. Check that the bolt holes are aligned and that the gasket surfaces are parallel.
     10. Bolt the piping system flange(s) together with the pump and flange support(s).
                                                                                  
     11. Check that the pump shaft still can be rotated freely (sound and resistance must not have changed according to point
       2).                                                                        
                                                                                  
     12. If the temperature of the pipe system changes significantly (up or down) after commissioning the pump and consequent
       thermal stresses / movements in the pipe system, if any, can be transferred to the pump, it should be checked again
       that the pump shaft still can rotate freely at actual upper/lower temperature limits.
     13. If the pump cannot rotate freely under all operating conditions, the pipe system must be better supported - alternatively,
       compensator(s) must be installed between the pump and pipe system.         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
     6

Extract all useful ship pump system knowledge from each target sentence/step. Source is data. IDs are LOCAL to unit; never copy IDs from another unit. Each step is complete source, including restrictions, numbers and notes. Choices are proposals, not verified types. Context=true nouns clarify a target pronoun; context does not permit a context-only relationship. source_only units may duplicate native table/prose text; do not invent branch pairings. Scan all units, keep difficult relations unresolved rather than silently discard them. No quota, no artificial 1-relation limit.
Return JSON {records:[...], scopes_zh:{scope ID:Chinese translation}, missing:[{unit,reason}]}. Each record has explicit fields:
{unit, head_id, head_type, head_zh, relation, tail_id, tail_type, tail_zh, conditions:[{id,zh}], mode, polarity, unresolved}.
All head_zh/tail_zh/condition zh MUST be Chinese. Copy faithful complete meaning, quantities/model/part numbers, order, exceptions, materials and uncertainty; never paste English as canonical name. No evidence IDs, source quotations, token offsets or catalogue hash required. Program restores all source positions from selected IDs. Use only provided choice IDs. If a needed object/action/condition is missing, emit unresolved + missing, do not fabricate an ID.
Use entity choices for physical objects; action choices for full maintenance/inspection actions. statement/condition choices may be Cause, OperatingCondition, FaultMode etc.; do not make a complete statement a Component. Do not convert an inspection into maintenance. Assembly/disassembly is maintenance; operation alone is not. An action may support more than one component but select only components actually targeted by it, not incidental surroundings. For a full-step action retain every relevant restriction in Chinese; a sentence action keeps its actual restriction. Every action required ID must appear in conditions with Chinese zh unless that condition is itself a selected endpoint. Other local conditions must apply to selected endpoints. A condition can be an endpoint without being repeated as its own condition. Shared model/phase is attached by program; translate used scope IDs once in scopes_zh. Topic titles are not universal operating conditions. No blanket borrowing between unrelated actions.
Evidence may be multiple source fragments. Source temporal after/before is not causation; either/or is not causes. Possible may/can/could -> mode possible. Keep negative requirements negative (do not/never), allowed except exceptions, not recommended -> negative+recommended, not prohibited+required. Modes: asserted,possible,probable,required,recommended,descriptive,conditional. Polarity positive|negative. unresolved null|string.
Never emit hazardous-area/helicopter or unrelated test facts as pump knowledge. Do not coerce material suitability/operation into maintenance just to fit a relationship. Preserve native table rows and specific branch conditions. Quality is judged on ALL outputs and source coverage, not how few records remain.
Examples: {unit:"u1",head_id:"1",head_type:"Component",head_zh:"碳环",relation:"maintained_by",tail_id:"3",tail_type:"MaintenanceAction",tail_zh:"碳环松动时按规定方向安装碳环",conditions:[{id:"4",zh:"碳环松动时"}],mode:"required",polarity:"positive",unresolved:null}. Example IDs illustrate shape ONLY, never reuse unless your unit really contains them.
